items.title: Bikies face Trump sanctions in 'Australian first' crackdown
paras: Southern Highlands-based Allan Meehan has been hit with sanctions by the Trump administration. ( Supplied )
Two Australians have found themselves in Donald Trump's sights as part of sanctions on the Comanchero bikie gang.
Allan Meehan and Marco Coffen face restrictions prohibiting American companies processing transactions for the pair.
The move comes as part of the Trump administration's crackdown on people connected to Mexican drug cartels.
Two Australians connected to the Comanchero bikie gang have been targeted by the Trump administration as part of a wider crackdown on Mexican drug cartels.
The sanctions handed to Allan Meehan and Marco Coffen overnight prohibit American businesses or residents conducting financial transactions with the pair.

The restrictions approved by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were part of sweeping prohibitions against the Comanchero and Italian gangsters the 'Ndrangheta, otherwise known as the Calabrian mafia.
"[Cartels] rely on other criminal organisations like the Comanchero and 'Ndrangheta to move drugs, launder illicit proceeds, and ultimately poison Americans with narcotics," Mr Bessent said.
Australia does not enforce US sanctions, but American businesses operating here may not process transactions for Meehan and Coffen, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said.
Assistant Commissioner Stephen Nutt says the move will "constrain" the Comanchero. ( ABC News )

"The Comanchero provides logistical support to some of the world's most dangerous cartels, including organisations designated by the United States as foreign terrorist organisations," AFP Assistant Commissioner Stephen Nutt said.
"[The] sanctions will constrain the Comanchero's access to the international financial system and increase the risks for those who enable or do business with it.
"Our objective is to make it harder, riskier and more expensive for the Comanchero to operate."
The crackdown is the first time an Australian-based crime gang has been sanctioned, the AFP said.
Meehan is considered by the US government to be the Comanchero "world president", but keeps a low profile from his Southern Highlands, NSW home.
This is despite reports earlier this year that Meehan and a Comanchero sergeant-at-arms had been removed from the gang over an internal squabble.
Allan Meehan has been a target of law enforcement since rising through the Comanchero ranks. ( ABC News )
Meehan rose to power within the Comanchero as its national president four years ago after several high-ranking members found themselves imprisoned.
A former member of the Rebels bikie gang before patching over, Meehan has emerged as a key focus of law enforcement since.
Meehan found himself a target of rarely used police powers in 2022, with NSW Police placing restrictions on his associations, his money and his movements.
Seeking to escape those restrictions on the Gold Coast, Meehan was taken back to Sydney in handcuffs to face charges for breaching them.
The NSW Police served Meehan with a Serious Crime Prevention Order at a time when the Comanchero were at war with Sydney's Ahmad crime family.
The feud saw three people shot dead: Omar Zahed, Mahmoud "Brownie" Ahmad and Rami Iskander.
Meehan is not accused of having any involvement in those attacks and has never been charged with or accused of drug offences related to Mexican drug cartels.
Less is known about Coffen, who is described by the AFP and the US Treasury as an associate of the gang.
Coffen has been overseas since 2013 and is a person of interest in the murder of security guard Gary Allibon, suspected to have been perpetrated by the Comanchero.
His name has also emerged in the years since in connection with running an encrypted phone network favoured by the underworld.
The Comanchero remain a powerful force in the Australian underworld. ( AAP: Dean Lewins, file photo )
The Comanchero are considered one of the most powerful bikie gangs in Australia, with a global footprint. They have been accused of orchestrating murders and large-scale drug importations.
Founded by Jock Ross in the 1960s, the Comanchero earned public infamy after the notorious Milperra massacre in 1984, which saw seven people killed in a shootout with the Bandidos bikie gang.
The AFP said Coffen and Meehan could face their bank accounts being closed, have trouble securing a home loan and scrutiny on their transactions.
Four of the gang's senior members and a key associate have also been sanctioned. ( Supplied: Australian Federal Police, file photo )
Financial institutions could also face penalties if found processing transactions on their behalf.
"This organised crime group floods our country with drugs, is responsible for violent crimes and murders, and peddles poison in our community and across the globe," Assistant Commissioner Nutt said.

"Members of the Comanchero live large, build wealth from the misery of others and undermine our safety and security, while law-abiding Australians work hard, pay tax and bust their guts to pay their bills from the money they legally earn."

items.title: ‘Pushing food around the plate’: How weight-loss drugs are changing what Australia eats
paras: The first GLP-1 weight-loss tablets arrive in Australia as chefs, supermarkets and fast-food chains rethink portion sizes and menus.
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A Celebrated restaurateur and cookbook author Karen Martini has seen all sorts of trends during her career. The latest, the explosive growth in use of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, leaves her perplexed.

“What I find most disappointing is groups of well-dressed, thinner men and women out to lunch or dinner, who still want the experience of going out, eating and drinking,” Martini says. “And all they do is push the food around the plates pretending to eat, usually ordering too much to compensate for not eating. I’ve seen this from time to time in restaurants in Melbourne, Sydney and Europe.”

Karen Martini says it’s disappointing when people don’t finish their meals. Eddie Jim It’s a sad state of affairs for all chefs making beautiful food, she says. “Every chef wants to please the diner and see flavours savoured, and clean plates sent back to the kitchen. We thrive on people enjoying food, rather than pushing it aside and not being able to finish.”

Australians are obsessed with health and longevity, but have an excess weight problem: official figures show 14.6 million of us are overweight or obese (67 per cent of adults and 27 per cent of children).

These excess-weight figures are tipped to tumble, however, as GLP-1 medicines become cheaper and easier to use. This month, the medicine regulator approved two weight-loss pills, Eli Lilly’s daily pill, marketed as Foundayo, and Novo Nordisk Pharmaceuticals’ Wegovy pill, which are set to make weight-loss treatments more attractive for many than the weekly injections available on the market so far. Wegovy will be available for sale on Friday; Eli Lilly says Foundayo will be available “in coming days”.

“I suspect we may look back on their impact on society and say it’s been one of the most significant changes in a long time,” says Ben Willee of Spinach Advertising, whose firm has done campaigns for food companies.

The drugs have evolved from treating diabetes to managing obesity. They reduce their users’ appetite and weight. But they also put them at higher risk of nutritional deficiency and muscle loss , and questions remain about their long-term side effects. Dietitians Australia president Dr Fiona Willer says weight is not the same as health, and she is concerned about the risk of malnutrition among users who don’t plan their meals or get monitored by a health professional.
“You get full on much less food than before, so every mouthful counts when you’re on these drugs,” she says.

Australia’s $160 billion food and grocery sector has found itself at the front line of this GLP-1 boom. Supermarkets, restaurants, meal-delivery businesses, cafes and fast-food chains are considering and changing their offerings, prices and portion sizes to capture a user market that – on one estimate – will grow to 30 per cent of adults, or 7 million people, within a decade.

Broadly, meals for users will be smaller, low-fat, low-spice and filling, with added protein (to prevent muscle loss) and added fibre (to aid digestion). At restaurants, smaller entrees and big plates of protein to share, such as lamb or steak, could become more popular, says Martini.

Eggs are a cheap and popular source of protein. Nine Pasta, dairy, and even rice are not immune to the protein obsession. Rice brand Sunrice says 28 per cent of Australians are seeking high-protein foods when they shop, which has prompted it to release a “Protein+ Rice” product with 10 grams of protein via “beef-derived collagen peptides”.

Australia is still at an early stage of the GLP-1 wave, says Rolf Weber, who leads meals-delivery business Marley Spoon. Twelve per cent of Marley Spoon’s sales are “GLP-1 support” meals, which are smaller, low in fat, have at least 20 grams of protein, six grams of fibre, and designed to be easy to digest.

GLP-1 drugs are subsidised through the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, but not for weight loss alone. People who want the drug for weight loss must pay hundreds of dollars a month, meaning disadvantaged people are either priced out of the life-changing medication or sacrificing other spending. One study found half a million people each month use it for type 2 diabetes, and more still for weight loss. A separate EY Studio+ survey found one in 10 Australian adults used them.

But regulatory approval of GLP-1 tablets (instead of a weekly injection) and the drug’s expected listing on the PBS for weight-loss purposes (slashing prices to just $25 a month) are tipped to ramp up demand.

“It will become more affordable – that means a higher uptake. It will reach some sort of ceiling eventually, but we’re far away from reaching that,” says Weber. He predicts, in time, 20 per cent of Australians will either be on weight-loss medication or taking a break from it.

Consultants EY-Parthenon forecast take-up will rise to 30 per cent in a decade if PBS approval expands to include GLP-1 use for weight loss and secondary morbidities such as hypertension and heart disease. Health Minister Mark Butler has described this class of drugs as “too important” not to have on the PBS, but there are concerns about how much this would cost. A spokesperson for the Department of Health says negotiations on a potential PBS listing for weight management were ongoing.

Next month, a decision will be released on expanding a PBS listing to obese patients with a history of heart attack, stroke or peripheral arterial disease. As yet, no company has sought subsidy through the PBS for weight-loss management alone. PBS listings typically take months, rather than years.

While food retailers do not know whether individual customers use a GLP-1 medication, supermarket giant Coles says protein-rich eggs and mince, fresh produce, fibre-rich foods, nutritionally balanced meals and hydration are increasingly popular among customers.

“For customers eating smaller portions, nutrient-dense foods and convenient meal solutions can also become more important, which is why we continue to look at opportunities across areas such as ready-made meals, pre-prepared fresh produce and salads,” a Coles spokesperson says.

Rival supermarket Woolworths says it’s expanded its range of protein- and fibre-rich food to meet increased demand, particularly protein-boosted options such as snack bars, yoghurts, milks and ready-to-eat meals.

Some fear widespread GLP-1 take-up will lead to fewer visits and lower revenue for a restaurant industry already slammed by the cost-of-living crisis and inflation (an EY survey found GLP-1 users reported they were dining out 44 per cent less). But not everyone is convinced that GLP-1s will lead to fewer meals out, or less money spent at hospitality venues.
Wes Lambert, the chief executive of the Australian Restaurant and Cafe Association, says GLP-1 take-up is still too low to meaningfully affect patronage and revenue.

Nonetheless, he says hospitality venues in high-income areas – where individuals can afford to pay upwards of $500 a month for GLP-1 treatment of non-diabetes-related weight loss – are reporting that diners are swapping unhealthy orders for high-quality items.

“Healthier things tend to cost more, so it is replacing quantity with quality,” he says. “Some venues around the country are indicating that they’ve noticed a small change. But it will take a decade or more, and wider use of GLP-1 medications, before we actually will see the outcome.”

The Australian Food and Grocery Council, which represents the food, beverage and grocery supply industry, describes GLP-1s as “another catalyst for innovation” among food manufacturers. “Eating less does not necessarily mean changing what we eat,” says chief executive Colm Maguire. “Research indicates consumers may look for smaller, more premium products, moments or occasions when they indulge, more protein and nutrients, and taking supplements to complement their diet.”

Even rice comes with added protein now. Craig Abraham Ganesh Kashyap, chief executive ANZ at Sunrice Group, agrees. He says GLP-1s sit “within a much broader set of changes in what consumers want, from greater interest in nutrition and protein to convenience and changing eating occasions. I don’t think the impact will necessarily come down to people simply buying less food, as consumers make choices based on a whole range of factors, from nutrition and value, to taste, convenience and occasion.”

Australia’s fast-food market has come under pressure from not only the GLP-1 trend and cost-of-living pressures, but rising company costs for wages and ingredients. The world’s biggest fast-food chain, McDonald’s, is now moving to push back by exploring GLP-1-friendly menu options.

McDonald’s USA president Skye Anderson told investors in September that customers on GLP-1 drugs want more protein and control over portions, so the burger and fries chain is looking at introducing items such as egg bites, burger bowls and a grilled chicken snack wrap, Forbes magazine reports. (McDonald’s and Hungry Jack’s in Australia did not respond to requests for comment).
As Anderson noted, customisation – the ability of customers to add, subtract and substitute ingredients as they wish – is highly sought after by nutrition-conscious customers.

Steven Marks, founder and co-chief executive of Australian chain Guzman Y Gomez (whose shares are up 26 per cent this year)says the Mexican food chain hasn’t changed its menu or portion sizes in response to changing health trends. “We are set to provide guests with choice – whether it’s adding double protein or extra guacamole, or choosing a mini size rather than a regular,” he says.
Setting GLP-1s aside, Australians will no doubt continue to focus on healthy food, encouraged by countless content creators on social media.

“This concept, that it’s not hard to eat healthily and prepare good food, is a really key theme of content creators. There are huge trends, especially on TikTok, in and around healthy eating. Cooking is fashionable again, and air fryers,” says Willee.
Karen Martini worries especially for young people, who might feel pressure to take the weight-loss route, and will therefore miss out on the joys and pleasure of food.
“Nutrition at this age is so important, and there will be massive health issues in large numbers of people earlier in life,” she says.

items.title: Sydney housing prices fall almost as fast as the Great Depression
paras: As housing prices continue to fall at the fastest rate in at least half a century across the nation, Australia recently recorded the largest price falls since at least 1980 at a five-capital-city aggregate.

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "C-295 facility represents work culture of New India," says PM Modi as he and Spanish PM inaugurate facility
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Vadodara (Gujarat) [ India ], October 28 (ANI): Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday inaugurated the TATA- Airbus aircraft assembly facility complex in Vadodara. The facility will manufacture C-295 aircraft at the TATA Advanced Systems Limited campus. PM Modi said that the C-295 facility represents the work culture of a new India . "Recently, we lost the country's great son Ratan Tata ji. If he had been among us today, he would have been happy, but wherever his soul is, he would be happy. This C-295 aircraft factory reflects the new work culture of New India ... When I was the Gujarat CM, it was decided to set up a factory in Vadodara to build train coaches. The factory was also prepared for production within a record time. Today, we are exporting the metro coaches manufactured in that factory to other countries. I am confident that in the future, the aircraft made in this factory will also be exported to other countries," PM Modi said. "Today the defence manufacturing ecosystem in India is touching new heights. If we had not taken concrete steps 10 years ago, it would have been impossible to reach this level today. At that time, no one could even imagine that there could be such large-scale defence manufacturing in India . But we decided to walk on the new path, set a new goal for ourselves. And today the result is before us," PM Modi added. The Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez underlined the importance of the new industrial site. Sanchez said, "Today we are not only officially inaugurating a cutting-edge industrial facility. Today we're also witnessing how an extraordinary project between two emblematic companies becomes a reality. Prime Minister Modi, this is another triumph of your vision. Your vision is to turn India into an industrial powerhouse and a magnet for investment and business. This partnership between Airbus and Tata will contribute to the progress of the India n aerospace industry and will open new doors for the arrival of other European companies." " Tata is probably the best exponent of India n industrial strength. Its products and services are present in virtually every country on the planet. Tata is a giant among giants. As for Airbus , it embodies the very essence of a united Europe. Committed to technological innovation and the creation of jobs and prosperity. For my country, for Spain , being an integral part of the Airbus consortium, defending the values it represents. Values on which the very idea of Europe is based on cooperation, modernity and progress," Sanchez added. During the inauguration of the TATA Aircraft Complex for manufacturing C-295 aircraft, Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran announced the facility's goals. "The final aircraft assembly complex for the first aircraft to be delivered is being set up here. I must commit to our Prime Minister that exactly two years from now we will deliver the first indigenously manufactured aircraft and we will request and we'll work with your office to block the date so that you can come and inaugurate the facility and receive the first product. The first 200 engineers from Tata Group are already in Spain going through the training that is required, and we have worked with 40 SME companies and we will be adding more companies to build the entire localisation that is required for the product," he said. This collaboration between Tata Advanced Systems Ltd. (TASL) and Airbus Spain will mark India 's first private sector final assembly line (FAL) for military aircraft, boosting the nation's aerospace capabilities. The plant, located at TASL's Vadodara campus, is part of India 's Rs 2.5 billion deal signed in 2021 to acquire 56 C-295 military transport aircraft from Airbus . Under the agreement, Airbus will deliver 16 aircraft directly from Spain , while the remaining 40 will be manufactured in India by TASL. This project will create a comprehensive ecosystem for aircraft development, covering assembly, testing, certification, and maintenance throughout the lifecycle of the aircraft. Major India n defence players like Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) and Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL), along with smaller enterprises, are also contributing to this project. The C-295 aircraft will strengthen India 's Air Force fleet with a modern and more reliable transport solution. Earlier in the day, PM Modi and Sanchez participated in a roadshow in Vadodara as they headed to inaugurate Tata Advanced Systems Ltd's facility. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up
paras: lobbying Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up Amazon now uses its shopping platform for political purposes.

55 ... ... ... A worker delivers Amazon packages in San Francisco, California, US, on Wednesday, Oct. 5, 2022. Credit: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images A worker delivers Amazon packages in San Francisco, California, US, on Wednesday, Oct. 5, 2022. Credit: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a New York City bill.
When I log into Amazon today, I’m met with a vertical banner that reads: “ATTENTION NYC Council could add up to $5 per order” with a button that says “Act now.”

The message is delivered as a pop-up for users of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn’t specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I’m logged into Amazon.

Amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518 ), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. If passed, it would require Amazon to directly employ the third-party delivery contractors that it uses.
Clicking on “Act now” on Amazon’s homepage or in the app brings up a page that gives shoppers a way to contact their NYC Council member and further states:

Right now, Amazon works with a network of small delivery businesses that are deeply embedded in your communities. If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city. That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.

It’s not unusual for Amazon to take a stance on political matters, and it has publicly opposed the Delivery Protection Act since April . What is new is Amazon using its online marketplace to push a political view. It’s uncommon to see a pop-up about legislation when visiting a shopping website.

The messaging suggests that Amazon is concerned about the potential impact the proposed law would have on its costs. Besides Amazon, the bill targets any company with last-mile delivery facilities in NYC, like FedEx and DoorDash.

It also raises questions about the potential impact on shoppers should Amazon expand its use of its e-commerce platform for additional political messaging. The pop-up launched today impacts only NYC residents but sets a precedent for Amazon to sway political views on other issues. Amazon has made similar moves internally, including reportedly using an app for its employees to campaign against unionizing. But the new pop-up shows Amazon extending that strategy directly to its users.
Given Amazon’s considerable influence in commerce, other companies could copy its actions. Uber and Lyft have previously done so, CNBC reports .

Finally, there’s the question of whether Amazon is fairly depicting the situations surrounding the bill. Notable supporters of the Delivery Protection Act include NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Amazon division of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters. Using a platform with massive reach to communicate only one side of an ongoing debate could lead to misinformation and a skewed public perception.

The Delivery Protection Act is currently stalled in the City Council’s Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection. The last hearing on the bill was in April. A committee vote on whether to advance the act to the full City Council hasn’t been set.

items.title: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows
paras: Priorities MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows Expert called MAHA’s spending “pretty unusual” for a PAC.

42 ... ... ... Credit: Getty | Scott Suchman Credit: Getty | Scott Suchman Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement’s midterm wipeout , a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA’s own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group’s priority was ever winning elections in the first place.
The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates.

The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA’s clout in the midterms . In reality, MAHA PAC took in $3.2 million. During the election cycle, the PAC spent more than $10.5 million, with over $7 million coming from money it had collected previously.

According to Stat’s findings, of the $10.5 million the MAHA PAC spent on the midterms, less than a tenth—roughly $1 million—went to messaging on political candidates, which are expenses called “independent expenditures.”
Andrew Mayersohn, a committees researcher at OpenSecrets, called the spending “pretty unusual,” explaining that “Major super PACs spend most of their money on independent expenditures.”

In some cases, the scant political spending was dwarfed by spending on luxuries. For instance, in a key House race in Northern California, MAHA supported Kevin Kiley over his political rival, pediatrician Richard Pan. Despite calling the race “the most direct ideological confrontation” between MAHA and its opposition “anywhere on the 2026 ballot,” the PAC only spent $49,900 to back Kiley. That’s a little less than the $50,100 it spent at Mastro’s Steakhouse, an upscale restaurant that offers $110 porterhouse steaks in Washington, DC. Further, it’s less than a third of the $155,900 the PAC spent at Ned’s Club, a luxury club near the White House that has become a popular gathering spot among Trump officials.

Of the roughly $1 million spent on political candidates, most of it—over $700,000—went to defeating Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.). Many other MAHA-endorsed candidates received $50,000 or less. Some got less than $2,000.

Outside of steaks and a private club, the MAHA PAC spent $500,000 on a media company, Merit Street Media, run by Phil McGraw, who hosted a MAHA special featuring Dr. Phil . MAHA leaders used PAC money to cover meals, payroll, and credit card bills. The PAC paid $275,000 to a security firm, Gavin de Becker & Associates, which is led by an ally of anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., MAHA’s top leader. Tens of thousands more went to LLCs that have little to no online information.

On the other hand, prominent online MAHA influencers also pocketed tens of thousands from the PAC, as did writers for The MAHA Report, a Substack that promotes Kennedy and MAHA interests. In the days after the midterms, as members of the movement were coming to grips with the election losses, The MAHA Report chose to publish a lengthy article defending convicted rapist Russel Brand , a Kennedy ally who became a MAHA fixture.
The biggest chunk of the MAHA PAC’s spending—more than $3 million—went to the nonprofit MAHA Action, which is also run by Lyons. It’s unclear how all that money was spent.

items.title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
paras: ON BEHALF OF THE “MOTHERLAND” Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say 25-year-old accused of stalking employees at coffee shop and in an “aggressive” car pursuit.

23 ... ... ... Credit: Getty Images | the-lightwriter Credit: Getty Images | the-lightwriter Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor.

Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday . He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.”

“FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.”

When police later questioned D’iu about the incident, the defendant allegedly said he saw a woman get into a car and thought she was “beautiful.” He then told the investigators that he followed her because he “wanted to ask her out on a date.”

Prosecutors didn’t name the company, but both Reuters and Bloomberg , citing unnamed people with knowledge of the case, identified it as Palantir. Ars is unable to confirm that reporting. Palantir representatives didn’t respond to an email seeking confirmation.

D’iu allegedly entered the US unlawfully in the summer of 2026 after being recruited by someone over Telegram. Prosecutors said the party gave D’iu a clandestine assignment to target employees of a large technology and defense company. D’iu received instructions, equipment, and financial support along with information that his work was on behalf of “the motherland.” His instructions were to collect information about the company because it was supplying weapons for use against Russian forces in Ukraine.

Prosecutors said D’iu traveled from Istanbul, Turkey, to Mexico City in June. He then crossed the border into the US and was instructed to buy laptops, cell phones, wireless networking equipment, and remote access software. Besides instructions to monitor company employees at the coffee shop, D’iu’s orders also included positioning his laptop at certain locations near the company so it could be remotely accessed in an attempt to collect information from company employees nearby.

D’iu allegedly obtained fraudulent identification documents to conceal his identity as he conducted his activities. The documents included a falsified California ID card, an altered US passport, and a Social Security card bearing the assumed name of “Hugo Landry Johns.” The passport was allegedly an authentic US passport that originally had been issued to someone elsewhere in the country. It was modified to display D’iu’s photograph and assumed identity.

D’iu was arrested on October 30 and remains in custody. He is charged with one count of Conspiracy to Act as an Agent of a Foreign Government, one count of Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, and one count of Interstate Stalking. If convicted for Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, he faces a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release. He faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release for each conviction on the other two charges.
D’iu had his initial appearance in federal court on November 2. He is next scheduled to appear in federal court on November 24.

items.title: She was the first woman ever to be inducted into the Tennis Hall of Fame over 70 years ago
paras: Ashleigh Barty is your 2026 International Tennis Hall of Fame inductee. Barty , whose retirement from the sport in 2022 stunned the tennis community, has joined the likes of Roger Federer, Maria Sharapova and Martina Hingis in the Hall of Fame.

The three-time major champion fought off competition from 2009 US Open champion Juan Martin del Potro and two-time Grand Slam champion Svetlana Kuznetsova – both of whom have missed out on joining the Hall of Fame for a second consecutive year. Around 72 years ago, the first players were inducted into the Tennis Hall of Fame: Oliver Campbell, Joseph Clark, James Dwight, Richard Sears, Henry Slocum, Malcolm Whitman and Robert Wrenn.

A year later, the first female player was inducted into the Hall of Fame. Sutton, from the United States, is a four-time Grand Slam champion across singles and doubles, and a former major mixed doubles finalist.

items.title: How far Jannik Sinner could drop in the rankings if he needs surgery as latest update given
paras: Jannik Sinner is reportedly travelling to America for a consultation on the knee injury that has kept him out of action since Wimbledon. The former world number one is off to America for a second opinion on his knee.

Sinner isn’t keen on surgery, although several members of his medical team believe it is an option worth considering, according to ‘ Quotidiano ‘. Sinner is said to be dealing with two issues, one with his iliotibial band and another with his lateral meniscus.

Only time will tell if they require surgery, but if he does, what would that mean for his ranking? It’s been 130 days since Sinner last played a match, defeating Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final. Missing the remainder of the 2026 season, Sinner failed to accumulate any more points after July.
items.impact: A full year on the sidelines would seem extreme, but if he does require surgery, don’t be surprised to see him miss at least January’s Australian Open.

items.title: “I hope I can play”: Fils ready to answer Monfils’ first Davis Cup call
paras: Nobody had heard him on the subject before, but his words, given in reply to a Tennis Majors question, will go straight to the ears of the FFT. Arthur Fils is “very happy” that Gaël Monfils is the new France Davis Cup captain , and says he will try to play as much as possible in the team competition France has not won since 2017.
The Frenchman spoke on Thursday in Turin, after the 6-4, 7-6(6) defeat to Alexander Zverev that ended his season. “I am very happy that Gaël is captain,” Fils said in French.
He described the newly retired Monfils as a big brother and an idol from his youth. Asked about his place in the team, he said: “I’m going to try to play as much as possible.

items.title: “A hell of a season”: Fils leaves Turin “at the level” and heads on holiday
paras: Knocked out after one set by Zverev, Fils ends his first ATP Finals with one win in three matches. He says he is “at the level” but must win those matches, and will switch off before discussing 2027 with his team.
Arthur Fils called his season “a hell of a season” and said Turin showed him “that I’m at the level, that’s for sure. Then after I need to win the matches.

“It was the first time I had to do something like this,” he said. “After the end of the first set I knew I was not going to go through anymore. But I said, you know what, just enjoy yourself.” In French, he said he “gave everything over one set” before “a bad game at 3-3, I gave the break”.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
